_about: Gerald's tips on Home, 8 a month, a mix of practical marketing tips for business owners and silly ones. Edit here, then run python3 tools/sync_gerald.py and python3 tools/build_app.py. No em dashes.

January: Send a thank-you to your five best clients from last year before they get buried in new-year email.
Ask for a referral in the same note as your thank-you. People say yes when they feel appreciated.
New year, new pizza. Update your signature pizza so it does not taste like last year.
Write down three clients who went quiet. Send each one a pizza and a simple question: how is the new year going?
Resolutions fail by February. Pizza is forever.
Book your follow-up meetings now. Put a booking link on your next-step button.
I tried a resolution once. It was to eat less pizza. I lasted nine minutes.
A short note beats a long one. Two sentences, then sign off.
February: Valentine's week is a great time to thank clients you love working with. Keep it friendly, not romantic.
Heart pepperoni says thank you without saying a word.
Pick one person who sent you business last year and thank them by name for the referral.
Use a gift code for a February offer, like a discount for booking before the month ends.
February is short. So is my patience for cold pizza. Send it while it is warm.
Groundhog Day rule: if you see your shadow, send six more weeks of thank-yous.
Spell their first name in pepperoni. People always stop and look.
Follow up within 48 hours of every new lead. Speed wins more than clever wording.
March: Spring cleaning: tag your People list so you can send the right pizza to the right group.
St. Patrick's Day is a fun excuse to reach out. Green toppings optional, good luck wishes required.
Send a pizza to a client who just hit a milestone. Watch for promotions and company news.
Ask happy clients for a review in your note, with a link on the next-step button.
I found a four-leaf clover once. It was basil. I put it on a pizza anyway.
Quarter ends soon. Thank your clients before they get busy closing out the books.
Add birthdays to People and Gerald will remember them for you.
Pizza is a circle. Circles have no end. Neither should your follow-up.
April: Tax season is stressful. A surprise pizza for a client buried in paperwork goes a long way.
Administrative Professionals' Day is coming. Thank the assistant who always gets you on the calendar.
Earth Day is a nice reason to send the Garden Veggie or go vegan for the day.
April Fools' tip: spell PRANK in pepperoni. Then send a real thank-you the next day.
Check your next-step button. One clear ask works better than three.
Spring is referral season. People are planning. Remind them you exist.
I do not believe in April showers. I believe in extra cheese.
Look at who opened your last pizza but did not book. A friendly follow-up could close it.
May: Teacher Appreciation Week and Nurses Week are in May. Thank the people who look after your clients and your family.
Graduation season: congratulate clients whose kids are graduating. They will remember you.
Mother's Day is a great time to thank the moms who run businesses with you.
Memorial Day is a time to honor, not to sell. Keep your note simple and sincere.
Mid-year is a good time to check in with clients you have not talked to since January.
Plant a seed. Send a pizza. Water both regularly.
Use personal pizzas for life moments and business pizzas for work moments. Your box changes to match.
I tried gardening. Everything I grew was basil. I am not complaining.
June: Father's Day is a good excuse to thank the dads in your network.
Juneteenth is a day to celebrate and reflect. Keep your note thoughtful.
Summer slows things down. Use the quiet time to send thank-yous you have been putting off.
Six months in: thank the clients who made the first half of the year great.
Sunscreen protects your skin. Thank-you pizzas protect your relationships.
Wedding season is here. Congratulate clients who are tying the knot.
Save a box preset for your most common occasion so it takes seconds next time.
I went to the beach once. A seagull took my pizza. We do not speak of it.
July: Fourth of July week is quiet in most inboxes. A fun pizza stands out.
Fireworks confetti makes any summer pizza feel like a celebration.
Pick a past client and send a just because pizza. No ask. Just thanks.
Halfway through the year is a great time to ask for testimonials.
Hot dogs are fine. Pizza is better. I will not be taking questions.
Connect your calendar so a pizza is ready the moment a meeting ends.
Keep a list of clients who send you referrals. Tag them so you can thank them as a group.
Too hot to cook? I will make the pizza. That is literally my job.
August: Back to school season: congratulate clients sending kids off to college.
Plan your year-end thank-yous now. December fills up fast.
Send a pizza after a proposal goes out. It keeps you top of mind while they decide.
A gift code with a deadline gets more people to act than one with no end date.
August is the Sunday of summer. Send a pizza to make it feel like a Saturday.
Check your People list for missing emails. A pizza cannot find someone without one.
Review the pizzas that got opened most. Do more of whatever those had in common.
I am not saying I invented summer vacation. I am saying I took a lot of it.
September: Labor Day is a nice moment to thank the people who work hard for you, like your team and your vendors.
September is the new January. Clients are back and planning. Reach out now.
Send a pizza to a client who started working with you this time last year. Happy client anniversary.
Spell the name of their project in pepperoni. It shows you were paying attention.
Pumpkin spice everything is coming. I have not decided how I feel about it on pizza.
Add work anniversaries to People and Gerald will send a pizza on the day.
Use one clear call to action per pizza. Book a call, leave a review, or claim an offer.
Fall leaves confetti is in season. Use it before it falls off the menu.
October: Send it within an hour of the meeting. It lands while they still remember the conversation.
Spell the main topic in pepperoni. It shows you were listening.
Halloween is a fun, low-pressure reason to reach out. Bats confetti is in season.
Boss's Day is in October. Thank the leader who gave you a chance.
Start your holiday list now. Clients who hear from you in early December remember you.
Check if they are vegan before you bake. I notice these things.
I dressed up as a pizza for Halloween. Nobody noticed. I was already a chef.
Use the next-step button for one clear ask, like booking a follow-up.
November: Thanksgiving is the easiest time of year to say thank you. Do not wait until December.
Small Business Saturday is a great reason to thank the small businesses you work with.
Veterans Day is about gratitude. A simple, sincere note is best.
Send your client thank-yous the week before Thanksgiving so they land before the holiday rush.
Gratitude is free. Pizza is close enough.
Use Send to a group with a holiday preset to reach your whole client list at once.
I am thankful for cheese, sauce and you. In that order. Kidding. Mostly.
Ask for a referral in your Thanksgiving note. People are in a giving mood.
December: Holidays are crowded. Send your client thank-yous in the second week of December so they stand out.
Use the Holiday Feast pizza and a snow confetti box for a festive touch.
Year-end is the perfect time to thank clients for the whole year, not just the last project.
Add a gift code for January bookings. It gives them a reason to start the new year with you.
I checked my list twice. Everyone is getting pizza.
Thank your vendors and partners too. They make your work possible.
Keep holiday notes inclusive. Happy Holidays works for everyone on your list.
Rest is part of the work. Schedule your last pizzas, then take a real break.
